title: Don't Make Me Think
author: Steve Krug
summary: A short, funny guide to web usability: why people scan instead of read, and how to design pages they never have to puzzle over.

title: Code
author: Charles Petzold
summary: How computers really work, built up from flashlights and Morse code to logic gates, memory and processors.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: Two systems drive the way we think: one fast and intuitive, one slow and deliberate. Kahneman maps where each leads us astray.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
summary: A psychiatrist's account of surviving the camps, and the therapy he built on one idea: that meaning, not pleasure, keeps us going.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
summary: Small, repeatable changes compound. A practical system for building good habits and breaking bad ones.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
summary: Private notes of a Roman emperor on duty, mortality and staying calm — written for himself, read for two thousand years.

title: The Bhagavad Gita
author: Eknath Easwaran (tr.)
summary: A clear modern translation of the dialogue between Arjuna and Krishna on the battlefield, with chapter introductions.

title: Freakonomics
author: Levitt & Dubner
summary: An economist looks at cheating teachers, sumo wrestlers and baby names to show how incentives explain everyday life.

title: Nudge
author: Thaler & Sunstein
summary: How the way choices are presented — defaults, order, framing — quietly shapes the decisions people make.

title: Poor Economics
author: Banerjee & Duflo
summary: Two Nobel-winning economists test what actually helps the world's poorest families, one small experiment at a time.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
summary: A tour of the universe and of the people who learned to read it, from ancient Alexandria to the space age.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
summary: Black holes, the Big Bang and the nature of time, explained for readers with no maths at all.

title: The Gene
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
summary: The history of the gene from Mendel's peas to gene editing, woven with the author's own family story.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
summary: Evolution seen from the gene's point of view, and why it can produce both selfish and generous behaviour.

title: Thinking with Type
author: Ellen Lupton
summary: A clear primer on letter, text and grid — the standard first book on typography for design students.

title: The Elements of Typographic Style
author: Robert Bringhurst
summary: A typographer's handbook on proportion, rhythm and the details that make text pleasant to read.

title: Grid Systems in Graphic Design
author: Josef Müller-Brockmann
summary: The Swiss master's method for building grids that bring order to posters, books and exhibitions.

title: Ways of Seeing
author: John Berger
summary: Seven essays on how we look at images — art, advertising and the people in them.

title: Interaction of Color
author: Josef Albers
summary: Exercises showing that colour is relative: the same colour changes depending on what surrounds it.

title: The Story of Art
author: E. H. Gombrich
summary: The best-known introduction to art history, from cave paintings to the twentieth century.

title: Indian Art
author: Partha Mitter
summary: Five thousand years of Indian art, from the Indus Valley to the modern era, in one compact survey.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
summary: Why doors confuse us and stoves trip us up. The founding text of human-centred design.

title: Persepolis
author: Marjane Satrapi
summary: A graphic memoir of growing up in Iran during the Islamic Revolution, told in stark black-and-white panels.

title: Logo Design Love
author: David Airey
summary: A working guide to creating identities that last, with case studies from studios around the world.

title: Graphic Design: The New Basics
author: Lupton & Phillips
summary: The building blocks of visual form — point, line, plane, rhythm, texture — with exercises from studio classes.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
summary: The prince of Denmark, a ghost and a revenge he can't bring himself to take.

title: The God of Small Things
author: Arundhati Roy
summary: Twins in Kerala and the small events that shape one family's tragedy. Booker Prize, 1997.

title: Midnight's Children
author: Salman Rushdie
summary: Born at the stroke of India's independence, Saleem Sinai's life is tied to the nation's own.

title: Gitanjali
author: Rabindranath Tagore
summary: Song offerings that won Tagore the Nobel Prize in 1913, in his own English translation.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
summary: A brief history of humankind: how one species came to run the planet through stories, money and empire.

title: City of Djinns
author: William Dalrymple
summary: A year in Delhi, peeling back the layers of a city rebuilt again and again over centuries.

title: The Discovery of India
author: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Written in prison in 1944, Nehru's reading of India's past, from ancient times to the freedom struggle.

title: India After Gandhi
author: Ramachandra Guha
summary: The story of the world's largest democracy from 1947 onward, told through the people who shaped it.
